How it's made

Handcrafted, so nothing wakes you

Most sleep videos are a short clip on repeat. You can hear the seam every few minutes, and once your ear finds it, it keeps finding it. Ours are built differently, one episode at a time, with one goal: nothing in ten hours should give your brain a reason to wake up.

  1. Real recordings

    Every nature sound starts as a real, licensed recording: rain on a tin roof, surf rolling against a cliff, a campfire on the sand. If a recording doesn't sound right, we find a better one. Brown noise is made fresh for each video, so it never repeats either.

  2. Cleaned by ear and by eye

    We listen to each recording all the way through and read its sound picture, line by line. Electrical hum, motor whine, distant traffic, voices, birds, thumps and passing cars come out, unless they're supposed to be there, like the soft hum of the city outside a rainy window.

  3. Balanced by hand

    When there's more than one sound, like fire and rain, we try a few mixes side by side and keep the one that feels most restful. Nothing is boosted or squashed to sound bigger.

  4. Never on repeat

    The recording is shuffled into long, gently overlapping pieces, with soft fades where they meet and slow, natural swells in the volume. There's no seam to catch, and the same moment never comes around twice in ten hours.

  5. No sudden jumps

    The volume is kept low and steady from start to finish, with a slow fade in and a slow fade out. A loud crack or pop is gently rounded off so it can't startle you awake.

  6. Drawn for each episode

    Every episode gets its own scene with Slumber in it, drawn and gently animated: rain on the glass, flickering firelight, rolling waves. The scenes are kept dark and calm, so they're easy to leave on all night.

Meet Slumber

Slumber has never once been awake on camera.

You'll find Slumber in every episode, curled up somewhere warm: on the bed while rain runs down the window, on the window seat while the waves roll in, under the Christmas tree, or by the fire in a log cabin. She's always asleep and always comfortable.

The idea is simple: if Slumber can sleep through it, so can you.

How to fall asleep with it

  1. Pick tonight's soundRain for most nights, fire when it's cold, brown noise or the fan when the house is loud.
  2. Turn it down lowJust loud enough to cover the noise around you. Lower is better for a whole night.
  3. Dim the screen and turn the phone overThe scenes are made dark on purpose, so they're easy to leave running.
  4. Let it runTen hours means it won't stop halfway through the night and wake you.

Questions

Why are the videos ten hours long?

So the sound covers a full night. A shorter video ends at 3 a.m., the room goes quiet and the silence wakes you.

Will an ad wake me up?

We turn off ads in the middle of our videos. YouTube may still show one at the very start, before you fall asleep.

Does it loop?

No. The sound is shuffled in overlapping pieces, so there's no repeating pattern for your ear to catch.

Can I use it for studying or my baby's nap?

Yes. Many people use these for focus, reading and naps. For little ones, keep the volume low and the device away from the crib.

Which one should I start with?

Try the "What's keeping you up tonight?" picker above. If you're not sure, rain on a tin roof is a favorite.
